title: Establishing Persistence in Manding for Information in Children With Autism
abstract: ABSTRACT Individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may require explicit instruction to learn how to mand for information when they encounter missing or unknown information. The current study expands the previous research on mands for information by assessing the persistence of mands (i.e., resistance to extinction). Three children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder were taught to perform two behavior chains and mand for information in a variety of ways. EO and AO trials were interspersed to ensure appropriately discriminated responding. During EO trials, an item was missing that was required to complete the chain. Each participant was required to mand “where is the [item],” obtain the item, and complete the chain to access the terminal reinforcer. During AO trials, all items needed to complete the chain were present; therefore, no mand for information was necessary. Training began using one item, in chain one. After responding met the mastery criterion, generalization probes were conducted on the untrained item in chain one and both items in chain two. Mands for information generalized to the untrained item and the untrained chain for all three participants.
